title: Final Fantasy X Was the First Final Fantasy You Could Hear
hook:
Nine numbered Final Fantasy games went by before a single character spoke a word out loud. In 2001 Final Fantasy X changed that, and it also gave us the laughing scene. Did that scene make you cringe or make you cry?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.

script: Did you know Final Fantasy X was the first Final Fantasy where the characters actually spoke out loud? Nine numbered games came and went with nothing but text on the screen. Then in July of two thousand one, Square released the tenth game on the PlayStation Two, and Tidus and Yuna had real voices. It was a hit right away. Square shipped more than two million copies in Japan and sold through ninety percent of them in the first four days. The game reached North America that December and passed a million copies there in about seven weeks. Those new voices also gave us one of the most famous scenes in gaming. Tidus and Yuna stand by the water and force out a long, painful fake laugh. People have argued about that scene for twenty five years. Producer Yoshinori Kitase later said it was meant to capture how embarrassing a new romance feels when you look back on it. In other words, the awkwardness was the point. The game also led to Final Fantasy X Two, the first direct sequel in the whole series. Together the two games have now shipped more than twenty million copies. So, did the laughing scene make you cringe, or did it make you cry? Follow for more gaming history.
